chullin-57b-9-10.note: Rabbi Shimon ben Halafta was known for testing things for himself. Reading in Proverbs that the ant has 'no chief, overseer, or ruler', he set out to see whether ants really have no king. On a hot summer day he spread his cloak over an ant hole to make shade and marked the one ant that came out. It went back in and told the others shade had come; they all came out, he lifted his cloak, and when the sun hit them they set on the marked ant and killed it. He concluded they had no king, since otherwise they would have needed the king's order to put it to death.
chullin-57b-9-10.why: The Gemara has been describing his experiments with sick hens to test which injuries are fatal, and asks how he earned the title 'researcher of matters'. This story answers, and the Sages then question whether the experiment proves anything.

people.name: Rabbi Shimon ben Halafta
people.about: A Sage of the Land of Israel around 200 CE, remembered for his experiments with animals.

people.name: Rav Mesharshiyya
people.about: A Babylonian Sage of the fourth century who explains the origin of Rabbi Shimon's title.

terms.meaning: A summer month in the Jewish calendar, roughly June to July, the hottest part of the year.

chullin-111a-4-4.note: Rav bar Shabba visited the home of Rav Nahman and was served cooked liver, but would not eat it. The household told Rav Nahman that a Torah student inside, Rav bar Shabba, was not eating. Rav Nahman told them: 'Feed it to Shabba', make him eat it whether he likes it or not.
chullin-111a-4-4.why: The Gemara is discussing whether cooked liver, full of blood, is permitted, and whether its blood spoils other food. Rav Nahman, whose own household poured boiling water on liver, shows here that he regarded such cooked liver as fully permitted.

people.name: Rav bar Shabba
people.about: A Babylonian Torah student who refused to eat cooked liver.

people.name: Rav Nahman
people.about: A leading Babylonian Sage and judge of the third and fourth centuries, in whose home the meal took place.
